items.text: Summaries are frequent, heavy and invisible

items.text: About 98% of the context replaced by a model-written summary each time
items.anchor: Each time about 98% of the context was replaced by a summary written by the model, and nothing told me what was kept.

items.text: A rule held only in conversation has to win every summary; when it does not, nothing tells you

items.text: Re-anchoring takes the rule out of the contest: rules are restored, not remembered

items.text: Re-anchoring fixes forgetting, not the other two failures; those need a second reader and a gate
items.anchor: **Re-anchoring fixes forgetting, not the other two failures.**

items.text: A canary makes the invisible visible: if the report stops appearing the person notices before anything important goes wrong

items.text: Compaction: in Claude Code, the harness writes a summary of the conversation when context fills and continues from it; manual or automatic
items.anchor: In Claude Code this is compaction, and it can be manual or automatic.
items.section: What summarisation does to a session

items.text: When the context fills, the harness writes a summary of the conversation and continues from the summary
items.anchor: When the context fills, the harness writes a summary of the conversation so far and continues from the summary.
items.section: What summarisation does to a session

items.text: Eighteen compactions between 9 September and 9 October, all automatic
items.anchor: Between 9 September and 9 October there were eighteen compactions, all automatic.

items.text: Each compaction started from about 780,000 to 800,000 tokens and kept 9,000 to 19,000; on average 1.7% kept
items.anchor: Each started from about 780,000 to 800,000 tokens of context and replaced it with 9,000 to 19,000: on average **1.7% kept**.
items.section: What summarisation does to a session

items.text: 17.8 million tokens of conversation summarised away in total
items.anchor: In total, 17.8 million tokens of conversation have been summarised away.

items.anchor: Each summary took between 1.2 and 3.4 minutes to write.

items.text: Summaries are not criticised: they make a month-long session possible, and the site would not exist in its current form without them
items.anchor: A summary is what makes a month-long session possible at all, and this site would not exist in its current form without it.

items.text: At every summary a conversational rule must be judged important enough to keep, in words the summariser chooses; you are not told when it fails
items.anchor: Every time a summary is written, the rule has to be judged important enough to keep, in words the summariser chooses.

items.text: Claude Code has four documented hook places to do re-anchoring
items.anchor: Claude Code has four documented places to do it ([hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)):
items.section: Re-anchoring: the rules come back from disk

items.text: SessionStart with matcher compact fires after every compaction and can print the whole policy back; its plain-text stdout is added to context
items.anchor: print the whole policy back: "Claude Code adds a SessionStart hook's plain-text stdout to Claude's context"
items.section: Re-anchoring: the rules come back from disk

items.text: UserPromptSubmit fires before each prompt, including harness-started turns, and can add a short anchor every turn or the full policy every Nth turn as additionalContext
items.anchor: add a short anchor every turn, or the full policy every Nth turn, as `additionalContext`
items.section: Re-anchoring: the rules come back from disk

items.text: PreCompact fires before compaction and can log it or block it
items.anchor: `PreCompact` | before compaction | log that it is about to happen, or block it
items.section: Re-anchoring: the rules come back from disk

items.text: Stop fires when the agent is about to end its turn and can check a required thing happened, sending the agent back once
items.anchor: check that something the policy requires actually happened, and if not, send the agent back once
items.section: Re-anchoring: the rules come back from disk

items.text: The SessionStart compact hook is the heart of re-anchoring: point it at the policy file and the policy is back verbatim when the summary is done
items.anchor: Point it at the policy file and the policy is back, verbatim, the moment the summary is done.
items.section: Re-anchoring: the rules come back from disk

items.text: Here the Agent Behaviour Policy stops being a document and becomes infrastructure: one file does three jobs
items.anchor: This is where the Agent Behaviour Policy stops being a document and becomes infrastructure.
items.section: One file, three jobs

items.text: Job 1, memory: the file is what the re-anchoring hook prints back; rules survive because they live on disk
items.anchor: The rules survive because they live on disk, not in the conversation.
items.section: One file, three jobs

items.text: Job 2, the checker's rulebook: the draft guard's numbered rule file, written by the inbox agent, is already an ABP fragment
items.anchor: The draft guard's numbered rule file, written by the inbox agent, is already an ABP fragment under another name.
items.section: One file, three jobs

items.text: Job 3, the enforcement list: every row carries its barrier, so the file says which rules still need a second reader or gate
items.anchor: Every row carries its barrier, so the file says which rules are still expectations, and therefore which need a second reader or a gate next.
items.section: One file, three jobs

items.text: A policy can shape memory directly with rows like keep decisions in decisions.md, moving important parts of a session into files
items.anchor: A row can say "keep decisions in `decisions.md`" or "write the sources file before drafting"
items.section: One file, three jobs

items.text: Such a row is still an expectation but a checkable one: a hook can see whether the file was written
items.anchor: That is still an expectation, but a checkable one: a hook can see whether the file was written.
items.section: One file, three jobs

flags: Total does not reconcile with per-compaction figures: eighteen compactions of about 780,000 to 800,000 tokens give about 14.1 to 14.4 million, but the article says "In total, 17.8 million tokens of conversation have been summarised away." (about 989,000 per compaction).

"one of the reasons was that the rule fell out of the agent's context when the conversation was summarised" and "a rule that had been written down four times" are asserted without evidence in this article; support lives in the linked a-second-reader article.
Superlative in the author's voice: "That sentence is the most important one I have read this week about running agents" (house style says no superlatives).

"The hooks this depends on arrived or changed in the last few months." Only mods (v2.1.287), onFailure (v2.1.295) and prompt-hook deny (v2.1.210) are versioned, with no dates; the compact matcher and SessionStart are not dated, so "last few months" is unsupported here.
Graph gaps: sources/re-anchoring-agent-behaviour-policies.graph.json links omit sources cited in the article: permission-modes docs, NPR and abp.sgit.ai.

Section 'Three ways a rule fails' names the three failures only in the figure caption ("Re-anchoring fixes forgetting. A second reader fixes the violation the author cannot see. A gate fixes the exception the agent argues itself into."); the prose never lists them, so the content depends on the image directive.
